meta.note: Editorial layer applied on top of the vendored HSK word lists (content/wordlists/). Those lists are mainland-standard: they carry traditional characters but PRC vocabulary and PRC readings. Spec §6 requires Taiwan usage throughout, so build_skeleton.py applies this file after loading a list and before binning words into lessons. Kept separate from the vendored lists so refreshing a list never clobbers these decisions.
meta.sources: Readings follow the Taiwan MOE 教育部重編國語辭典. Vocabulary substitutions follow everyday Taiwan usage per spec §6.

vocabulary.note: PRC word -> Taiwan word. The HSK list entry is replaced wholesale: the Taiwan form becomes the taught word, and the PRC form is recorded in taiwan_note so the learner can still recognise it.

substitutions.note: 台灣說「腳踏車」；「自行車」是大陸用法。
台灣說「計程車」，口語也說「小黃」。
台北、高雄等地的地鐵系統叫「捷運」。
台灣說「番茄」；「西紅柿」是大陸用法。
台灣說「列印」；「打印」是大陸用法。
台灣說「品質」；「質量」在台灣指物理的 mass。
台灣少用兒化，說「一下」或「等一下」。

canonical_forms.note: The vendored lists carry every spelling of a word in `forms`, and the first one is frequently not the standard Taiwan form. Three failure classes were found across the 79 multi-spelling entries: (A) forms[0] is an archaic variant — 咊 for 和, 㼝 for 碗, 嵗 for 歲; (B) forms[0] is the SIMPLIFIED form, which must never reach a traditional-only app — 听 for 聽, 几 for 幾, 从 for 從; (C) forms[0] is correct and the alternates are archaic or a different word — 吃/喫, 了/瞭, 你/妳. No heuristic separates these reliably, so the A and B cases are pinned here by simplified form. Anything absent keeps forms[0].

why_selected.里: Taiwan writes 裡 (not 裏) for the locative suffix.
why_selected.干: HSK 干 is 'dry' — 乾 in traditional. 干 alone is a different word (to offend).
why_selected.当: HSK 当 is dāng 'when / to serve as' — 當. 噹 is the onomatopoeia.
why_selected.脏: HSK 脏 is zāng 'dirty' — 髒. 臟 is zàng, an internal organ.
why_selected.复习: Taiwan MOE writes 複習 for 'to revise'.
why_selected.联系: Taiwan writes 聯繫 (not 聯係).

readings.note: Taiwan readings that differ from the PRC standard in the vendored lists. Two kinds: (a) outright different readings named in spec §6, and (b) the systematic case where the mainland standard neutralises a second syllable that Taiwan keeps fully toned (朋友 péngyǒu, not péngyou). Only words verified against Taiwan MOE are pinned here; the rest are listed under `needs_review`.

core.note: High-frequency words where the grammatical reading carries few dictionary senses but dominates real usage, so no sense-count heuristic finds it. 了 resolved to liǎo ('to finish') over le (the aspect marker); 那 to the archaic nuó; 沒 to mò ('drowned'); 嗎 to má. These are the most common words in the language and must be pinned.

corrections.note: Errors found in the hand-authored content, fixed here so the fix survives a re-import.

好吃.why: 好吃 meaning 'tasty/delicious' is hǎochī. hào chī (4th tone) means 'fond of eating'. The curated entry was glossed 'tasty; delicious' with the example 這個菜很好吃, so the reading was wrong — it was also feeding the wrong audio to TTS and the wrong target to tone training.

needs_review.note: Polyphonic words and mainland-neutralised readings that build_skeleton.py could not resolve with confidence. The Claude theming pass (--theme claude) resolves these per word in context; until then the vendored list reading is used. Run `python -m scripts.build_skeleton --report-readings` to regenerate this list.
